violations.text: Salsa kept in the 2-door refrigeration unit was observed with mold. Person in charge voluntarily disposed of item at the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 07/16/2026

Various foods were observed held at 40-47 degrees Fahrenheit in the 2-door refrigerator. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be held at 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below except during preparation, cooking, or cooling. Foods kept in the unit overnight and over 45 degrees Fahrenheit were voluntarily disposed of. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 07/16/2026

The 2-door refrigerator was observed in poor repair (maintaining an ambient temperature of 43 degrees Fahrenheit). The unit is to not be used for TCS foods until it can be replaced/repaired/serviced. Repeat Violation. Correct By: 07/16/2026

Food contact surfaces of equipment/utensils (ice machine) was observed with an accumulation of black residue. The food contact surfaces of equipment must be clean to sight and touch. Ice was voluntarily disposed of at the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 07/02/2026

Various food items were observed held at 44-47 degrees Fahrenheit in the 2-door reach in refrigerator. The ambient temperature of the reach-in refrigerator was observed at 50 degrees Fahrenheit. TCS foods kept in the unit over 4 hours were voluntarily disposed of. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be held at 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below except during preparation, cooking, or cooling. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 07/02/2026

The 2-door reach in refrigerator was observed in poor repair (maintaining ambient temperature above 41 degrees Fahrenheit). Unit is to not be used for any TCS foods until it can be repaired/replaced/serviced. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 07/02/2026

Soap was not available at the hand-washing sink located in ware washing area at time of inspection. PIC refilled soap at time of inspection. Hand-washing sinks must be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 06/23/2026

Food contact surfaces of equipment/utensils (can opener) were observed with an accumulation of food and debris. PIC relocated can opener to dish washer to be washed, rinsed and sanitized. The food contact surfaces of equipment must be clean to sight and touch. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 06/23/2026

The following foods were prep 6/22/26: slices of key lime pie, cole slaw and steak and held at (46-54) degrees Fahrenheit. All the food mentioned above was voluntarily disposed of at time of inspection. All other foods prepped today and held in refrigeration less than 4 hours was moved to walk-in cooler at time of inspection. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be held at 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below except during preparation, cooking, or cooling. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 06/23/2026

Proper cooling methods were not used for time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods. Per interview of (PIC), (eggs were cracked and prepped 3 hours prior to inspection in containers greater than four inches deep.) PIC removed lids and placed them in colder unit. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 06/23/2026

ROP frozen salmon (37 degrees Fahrenheit) observed completely thawed with package intact located in walk-in refrigerator. Frozen ROP seafood products that bear a label “keep frozen” must be completely removed from reduced oxygen packaging once taken out of the freezer to thaw or is stored in refrigeration holding an ambient temperature of 37 degrees Fahrenheit or below. PIC instructed staff to removed salmon from original package and repackage it in a container then placed back into walk-in cooler at time of inspection. Proper ROP seafood thawing reviewed. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 06/23/2026

Observed economy 2-door refrigerator located across from the service area was in poor repair/in need of an adjustment (not holding adequate ambient temperature). PIC instructed to not store TCS foods in refrigerator until service is provided/or unit is adjusted. -Hand-washing sink located in front area observed leaking and pooling water underneath. PIC cleaned pooling water at time of inspection. Front area has two other hand-washing sinks that they can use. Prep unit located next to hand-washing sink has broken handle in need of repair. Equipment shall be maintained in good repair. New Violation. Correct By: 07/07/2026

The following equipment has an accumulation of dust, dirt, residue, and other debris: -screens in windows located in prep area -fan located in ware washing area -fan covers located in walk-in cooler non food contact surfaces shall remain clean to sight and touch New Violation. Correct By: 06/23/2026
The hand sink at the bar was observed being used as a dump sink. A hand-washing sink must not be used for purposes other than hand washing. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 06/12/2025
Molluscan Shellfish tags did not have all of the required information. Last date of sale were lacking. New Violation. Correct By: 06/12/2025

Raw animal foods (such as eggs) were observed stored above ready-to-eat foods (such as bread and boiled eggs) in the Sautee reach in refrigerator. Raw animal foods must be separated from raw ready-to-eat food such as vegetables during storage. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 06/12/2025

Various foods in the Sautee prep unit was observed held at 45-52 degrees Fahrenheit. The sautee prep unit was observed maintaining an ambient temperature of 44 degrees Fahrenheit and unplugged. Per PIC, foods were kept in the unit overnight. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be held at 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below except during preparation, cooking, or cooling. Person in charge voluntarily disposed of foods at the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 06/12/2025

The following was observed to be thawing improperly: 1) Reduced oxygen packaged seafood (mussels, lobster, tuna, mahi mahi) was observed thawing the package in-tact. ROP seafood must be removed from the packaging upon thawing. The items observed over 38 degrees were voluntarily disposed of at the time of inspection. 2) Frozen meat was observed thawing on the counter. Food was moved to refrigeration to properly thaw. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 06/12/2025

The following was observed improperly stored: 1) A knife was stored in-between the prep table and the prep unit 2) Utensils were stored in stagnant water Utensils were relocated at the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 06/12/2025

The following was observed draining improperly: 1) Condensation was observed pooling at the bottom of the dairy cooler in the kitchen. 2) Condensation was observed dripping from the fan in the sautee cooler. Condensate drainage and other nonsewage liquids must drain into a drain. New Violation. Correct By: 06/26/2025

Shellfish tag(s) were observed not marked with the last date of use. Shellfish tags must be maintained for 90 days in chronological order AND the date when the last shellfish was used from the bag must be noted on the shellfish tag. Repeat Violation. Correct By: 07/02/2024

Raw animal foods (whole shell eggs) were observed stored above ready-to-eat foods in the walk-in refrigerator. Raw animal foods must be separated from raw ready-to-eat food such as vegetables during storage. Corrected On-Site. Repeat Violation. Correct By: 07/02/2024

At the time of inspection, all items on the menu (poached eggs) were observed not marked with an asterisk alerting to the consumer advisory. The consumer advisory provided must disclose the foods on the menu that are raw or undercooked. Repeat Violation. Correct By: 07/02/2024

Proper cooling methods were not used for the following time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods... - Pasta was observed cooling in a covered plastic container at 47 degrees Fahrenheit. Pasta was adjusted for rapid cooling at the time of inspection. - Recently prepped Hummus was observed cooling in a large, covered plastic container. Proper cooling methods were discussed with the PIC at the time of inspection. Food items are to be arranged in the EQUIPMENT to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls and loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination. Corrected On-Site. Repeat Violation. Correct By: 07/02/2024

Shellstock (oysters) located in walk-in cooler did not have the proper identification tags. Shellstock tags must remain attached to the container in which the shellstock are received until the container is empty. The person in charge contacted the vendor and got a copy of the oyster tags during time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 06/20/2024

Raw animal foods (such as fish) were observed stored above ready-to-eat foods (such as cooked lobster, cooked mussels, and cooked chicken) in the walk-in refrigerator. Raw animal foods must be separated from raw ready-to-eat food such as cooked lobster, cooked mussels, and cooked chicken. New Violation. Correct By: 06/20/2024

Food contact surfaces of equipment/utensils (slicer and can opener) were observed with an accumulation of food and debris. The food contact surfaces of equipment must be clean to sight and touch. New Violation. Correct By: 06/20/2024

Chicken was observed held at 49 degrees Fahrenheit in the walk-in cooler. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be held at 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below except during preparation, cooking, or cooling. Per person in charge, chicken had been in the walk-in cooler since the day prior. Chicken was voluntarily disposed of (see attached disposal form). Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 06/20/2024
The consumer advisory provided does not disclose the foods on the menu and menu board at the bar that are raw or undercooked. New Violation. Correct By: 06/27/2024

Proper cooling methods were not used for time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods. Per interview of bean salad was placed hot in the refrigerator in containers greater than four inches deep. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 06/20/2024

Reduced oxygen packaged (ROP) seafood (mussels), labeled keep frozen, were observed thawing with the package intact. ROP seafood must be removed from the package when thawing. Mussels were observed stored at 39-43 degrees Fahrenheit during time of inspection. Mussels were voluntarily disposed of (see attached disposal form). Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 06/20/2024

The door to the outside, located in the back kitchen, is not tight-fitting. Outer openings of a food establishment must be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by tight-fitting doors. New Violation. Correct By: 06/27/2024
The can opener was not in good repair. Can opener blade was rusty. Repeat Violation. Correct By: 06/27/2024

The sink used for food preparation is lacking an air gap. A direct connection must not exist between the sewage system and a drain originating from equipment in which food is placed. New Violation. Correct By: 06/27/2024
The floor in the basement area has an accumulation of pooled water. The physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. New Violation. Correct By: 06/20/2024
The walk-in cooler was observed improperly sealing due to gasket in poor repair. Person in charge stated that a maintenance service has been scheduled. New Violation. Correct By: 08/01/2023

The following is lacking a backflow prevention device: 1) The blender at the outdoor bar observed draining into a container 2) The prep sink was observed with an air-break - An approved backflow prevention device is required in order to prevent backflow of a solid, liquid, or gas contaminant into the water supply at each point of use at a food establishment. PIC stated that a maintenance visit has been scheduled for repairs/service/replacement. New Violation. Correct By: 08/01/2023
